items.text: An annuity is not a savings account and not life insurance. It converts a lump sum into income, usually for life. That trade can be right or wrong for you, and the deciding factor is liquidity, not the rate. honorbrook-insurance.com

Annuities get sold on the rate. The rate is rarely the thing that determines whether one was a good idea.

What an annuity actually does is convert money you have into income you will receive, often for as long as you live. That is a real solution to a real problem, which is not knowing how long retirement will last. It is also, structurally, a trade of access for certainty.

So the first question is not what it pays. It is what you give up. Most contracts limit how much you can withdraw in the early years without a surrender charge, and those schedules can run several years. If there is a reasonable chance you will need that money for a roof, a car, or helping family, an annuity is the wrong container for it, no matter how good the rate looks.

The second question is which kind. Fixed, indexed and immediate annuities behave differently enough that grouping them under one word causes most of the confusion in the category.

We will tell you when the answer is that you do not need one. That happens often.

Honorbrook Insurance, Tysons VA. honorbrook-insurance.com
